body.statement: Using the handle in \(\mathrm{def:implementation-handle}\), construct one jointly measurable schedule of pilot tolerances, dyadic depths, state nets, Gaussian observation rectangles, and probability enclosures that uses the fixed arm-within-stratum coordinate order, the lexicographic order on \(\{0,1\}^{2K}\), and the closed-boundary tie convention defining \(\mathcal D_k^\dagger\) and \(\mathcal C_k^\dagger\). At depth \(k+1\), the schedule must select the lexicographically first eligible child only among children of the unique ambient box selected at depth \(k\), with every child containing a shared-boundary point tested separately and no unrelated cell eligible. Prove that every fixed empirical tree prefix stabilizes to \(\mathcal D_k^\dagger\), hence its feasible cell stabilizes to \(\mathcal C_k^\dagger\), and that \(\lVert\widehat r_n-r^\dagger\rVert=O_P(a_n(L))\) locally uniformly for a deterministic law-specific rate \(a_n(L)\) derived from the certified prefix-separation profile, including disconnected, flat, tied, and dyadic-boundary minimizing sets, while the implemented rectangle rule has risk error \(o(1)\) uniformly over each bounded nuisance fiber; characterize whether any uniformly faster rate is impossible without an additional optimizer-identification modulus.
body.justification: This is the unresolved implementation theorem: set convergence alone does not select a deterministic representative, determine its attainable rate, or control a changing discontinuous decision rule.
body.gap: McIsaac and Cook learn a pilot-optimal allocation, Luedtke and van der Laan analyze exceptional decision laws, and Higbee assumes uniqueness and strong curvature; none supplies the required coupled selector and law-specific rate at nonunique optima.
body.consumer: The result turns the population minimax design into a pre-specifiable two-wave protocol that remains valid when several annotation designs are exactly tied.
